correctness.rationale: The mass Gram matrix is (6n)^{-1} times a strictly positive circulant tridiagonal matrix A with diagonal 4 and neighbor 1 (including n=3). The Green recurrence 4g_j+g_{j-1}+g_{j+1}=delta_{0j} has summable solution (-q)^|j|/(2sqrt(3)), q=2-sqrt(3); periodization gives the exact inverse A_n. Differencing rows 1 and 0 yields a signed derivative hat kernel, and L-infinity/L1 duality gives the sharp norm attained by the sign of that kernel. Nodal sign alternation (one exact zero for odd n) makes absolute affine-cell integrals equal the displayed cyclic rational expression, without vanishing denominators. The infinite signed kernel has exact absolute integral (9-sqrt(3))/2 from a central crossing plus geometric tails. The finite kernel is its absolute-convergent periodization, where cancellation of opposed copies on a positive-length subinterval makes strict inequality; the tail bound on a centered length-n interval is O(q^(n/2)). These analytic facts prove all n>=3, not merely numerically tested n.
